name: Proper Ordered Sample Compression
definition: The **Proper Ordered Sample Compression** is the minimum size of an order sample compression scheme whose decoded hypotheses all belong to $\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: Order-compression size with reconstruction constrained to the class.
origin_references: Order compression schemes were introduced by Darnstädt, Kiss, Simon, and Zilles in \cite{darnstadt2016order}; this is their proper-reconstruction restriction.

p_monotonic.proof: Project every compressed sample and every decoded hypothesis of a proper ordered scheme to the retained coordinates. The projected reconstruction remains a member of the projected class and the projected order is an order scheme of no larger size. This is the projection argument in Darnstädt--Doliwa--Simon--Zilles \cite{darnstadt2016order}.

c_monotonic.proof: Restriction to a conditioned fibre commutes with an ordered proper compression scheme after fixed coordinates are removed from its sample and reconstruction.
